evals.name: clear-commodity-finding
evals.expected_output: Flags ApiClient's hand-rolled retry loop as a finding: no decision evidence found (checked comment, ADR, commit history, project memory), resembles the general retry/backoff commodity pattern, recommendation is to re-run build-vs-adopt (not to prescribe a specific replacement).
expectations: Flags app/clients/api_client.py's retry loop as a finding
States what was checked for a decision and that none was found, matching the fixture
The recommendation is to re-run the build-vs-adopt evaluation, not a prescribed library replacement

evals.name: justified-custom-not-flagged
evals.expected_output: Does not flag SpendGovernor as a finding: it's domain-specific (contract-anniversary reset, mid-cycle override) and has an on-record ADR explaining why slowapi (a rate-limiting library already a dependency) doesn't fit. Lists it under 'considered, not flagged.'
expectations: Does not list SpendGovernor as a finding
Discusses it under 'considered, not flagged', citing the domain-specific behavior and/or the existing ADR
Does not recommend replacing SpendGovernor with slowapi or a similar rate-limiting library/service

evals.name: mixed-repo-discrimination
evals.expected_output: In one pass: flags LocalCache (undocumented, generic LRU/TTL cache used for a generic purpose) as a finding, and does not flag apply_tier_pricing (tightly coupled to Contract.tiers, has an inline rationale comment).
expectations: Flags app/cache/local_cache.py's LocalCache as a finding
Does not flag app/pricing/tier_calculator.py's apply_tier_pricing as a finding
Both determinations are correct in the same response

evals.name: weak-preference-evidence
evals.expected_output: Still flags NotificationDispatcher's hand-rolled retry loop as a finding even though a comment exists, because the comment states a preference/outcome ('simpler than adding a dependency') rather than showing a considered tradeoff. Evidence is characterized honestly as preference-only, not 'none found' and not sufficient to clear the candidate. Recommendation is still to re-run build-vs-adopt, not a prescribed replacement or an assertion the custom code is wrong.
expectations: Flags app/notifications/dispatcher.py's retry loop as a finding despite the existing comment
Characterizes the comment as preference-only / not showing a considered tradeoff, rather than reporting 'no evidence found' or treating it as sufficient to clear the candidate
The recommendation is to re-run the build-vs-adopt evaluation, not a prescribed replacement, and does not assert the existing implementation is wrong
